task_production_rates.name: Install full floor protection below ceiling work zone
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Full floor coverage with canvas drop cloths or builder's paper. Standard floor protection rate — this is floor-level work, NOT overhead. Spray only. Significantly more SF than wood wall's floor_perimeter (full room vs runners).

task_production_rates.name: Install perimeter floor protection at ceiling work zone
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Canvas drop cloth runners along work path. Floor-level work. Brush only. Same rate as wood wall floor protection.

task_production_rates.name: Mask upper wall band at ceiling-wall junction
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Tape + 12-24 inch masking paper or pre-taped film at ceiling-wall junction, extending down wall surface. Near-overhead work at junction height. Spray only. Inverse of wood wall's ceiling masking.

task_production_rates.name: Mask ceiling-mounted fixtures
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. Tape and plastic bag over each ceiling fixture. Overhead work — working above head to mask each fixture. Always required. Standard fixture masking rate.

task_production_rates.name: Install lightweight opening covers
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Quick pin-up of lightweight plastic over window/door openings. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Dust and clean all wood ceiling surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Overhead work — tack cloth or damp wipe all ceiling panel/board faces overhead. Longer than wood wall (20 min) due to full overhead posture for entire task. Board-style ceilings: clean groove channels overhead.

task_production_rates.name: Sand wood ceiling per substrate and state
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rates (SS_BARE: 100→75, SS_PRIMED: 150→110). Overhead sanding is the most fatiguing prep task — pole sander strongly recommended. Binary. Rate applies to flat_plank baseline — apply ceiling_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Fill fastener holes and minor defects

QT3.notes: Fill obvious holes only — overhead spackle application slower

QT5.notes: Fill every hole, check with angled light overhead

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rates (QT3: 120→90, QT4: 100→75, QT5: 80→60). Overhead spackle application is messier — use thicker spackle. Board-style ceilings have high fastener density.

task_production_rates.name: Sand filled areas smooth

QT4.notes: Sand flush overhead, visual check each fill

QT5.notes: Sand flush overhead, angled light verification

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rates (QT3: 150→110, QT4: 120→90, QT5: 80→60). Rigid sanding block for flat surfaces. Overhead sanding generates dust that falls onto worker.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk board or beam-panel joints

flat_plank.notes: Board-to-board butt joints — moderate density, overhead

beadboard.notes: Board-to-board bead groove joints — highest density, overhead

tongue_and_groove.notes: Board-to-board tight joints — high density, overhead

coffered.notes: Beam-to-panel inside corner junctions — complex orientation, overhead

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Internal joint caulk. Binary. Overhead penalty ~0.70x of wood wall rates (wall: 45-50→ceiling: 30-35). Overhead caulking is SIGNIFICANTLY harder — gravity pulls caulk from joints, requires thicker caulk and faster tooling. Beadboard has highest joint density overhead. Default rate_per_hour (32) is weighted average.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk ceiling-to-wall junction perimeter
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Perimeter caulk at ceiling-wall junction. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 120→ceiling: 90). ~0.5 LF perimeter per SF of ceiling area. Overhead — caulk at junction requires working at ceiling height.

task_production_rates.name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 60→ceiling: 45). Detail work overhead — shellac/oil sealer on cut/routed MDF edges. Sealer runs/drips from overhead edges. Apply in thin coats. Conditional: substrate=mdf AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Binary. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime.

task_production_rates.name: Prime wood ceiling surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 120→ceiling: 90). Full primer coat overhead. Binary — primer application quality not tiered. Conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. Lighter coats overhead to prevent sags. Apply ceiling_style modifier.

task_production_rates.name: Light sand primer for finish coat adhesion
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 150→ceiling: 110). 220 grit light sand overhead — pole sander for field. Binary. Apply ceiling_style modifier for profile complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Spray finish coat on wood ceiling
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat_plank at baseline. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 175→ceiling: 130). Spray ergonomics overhead are better than brush — overhead penalty may be closer to 0.78x for spray. Apply ceiling_style modifier: beadboard ÷1.15, T&G ÷1.10, coffered ÷1.35. Binary. Lighter coats overhead to prevent sags and groove pooling.

task_production_rates.name: Brush finish coat on wood ceiling
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr for flat_plank at baseline. Overhead penalty ~0.70x of wood wall rate (wall: 70→ceiling: 50). Brush overhead is more fatiguing — arms above head, more frequent rest intervals, brush drips on worker. Overhead penalty more severe for brush than spray. Apply ceiling_style modifier. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Clean work area between coats
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. Floor-level cleanup. Same as wood wall — cleaning floor protection is not overhead work.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect previous coat

QT3.notes: Quick glance from floor — overhead inspection inherently less detailed from distance

QT4.notes: Systematic scan from step ladder overhead

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection overhead from scaffold/ladder with angled light — zero tolerance

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rates (QT3: 400→300, QT4: 200→150, QT5: 100→75). Overhead inspection requires angled light to reveal defects — looking up.

task_production_rates.name: Sand between coats

QT3.notes: Spot sand nibs overhead — pole sander

QT5.notes: Thorough 220-320 grit overhead — most fatiguing interstage task

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rates (QT3: 200→150, QT4: 120→90, QT5: 80→60). Overhead sanding is especially fatiguing — dust falls on worker. Rigid block on flat surfaces, flexible sponge for grooves/corners.

task_production_rates.name: Patch and repair marked defects
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled — scope of repair increases with tier. Overhead patching — longer than wood wall (QT3: 5→7, QT4: 15→20, QT5: 25→30) due to overhead position making patching slower and messier.

task_production_rates.name: Spot coat patched areas
task_production_rates.notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Overhead touch-up — longer than wood wall (QT3: 5→7, QT4: 10→12, QT5: 15→20) due to overhead working position.

task_production_rates.name: Tack cloth all wood ceiling surfaces
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rate (wall: 200→ceiling: 150). Per interstage cycle. Overhead tack cloth work — arms above head for entire task. Work into grooves and corners. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Final quality inspection

QT3.notes: Scan from floor for obvious defects

QT4.notes: Systematic review from step ladder overhead

QT5.notes: Critical lighted overhead inspection with angled light

task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. qt_scaled. Overhead penalty ~0.75x of wood wall rates (QT3: 500→375, QT4: 250→190, QT5: 120→90). Overhead inspection requires angled light — inherently more difficult than wall inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Overhead touch-up — longer than wood wall (QT3: 5→7, QT4: 15→20, QT5: 25→30). QT5 may require full additional coat overhead if defects are widespread.

task_production_rates.name: Remove wall upper band masking
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Masking removal near ceiling height. Score tape edge before removal. Binary. Spray only.

task_production_rates.name: Remove opening covers
task_production_rates.notes: Per room. Quick teardown of lightweight plastic from openings. Spray only. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Remove fixture masking
task_production_rates.notes: EA/hr. Overhead work — remove tape and plastic from ceiling fixtures. Faster than setup (removal is simpler). Always required. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Remove floor protection
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Floor-level work. Fold canvas/paper inward to contain debris. Binary. Same rate as wood wall.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum work area
task_production_rates.notes: SF/hr. Floor-level work. May have more dust to vacuum than wood wall due to overhead sanding debris. Binary.

task_production_rates.name: Clean tools and equipment
task_production_rates.notes: Per session. Same as wood wall — tool cleaning is not overhead work. Binary.

H1_STANDARD.description: Standard ceiling height. Step ladder for overhead brush work. Basic overhead penalty already in base rates.

H2_STEP.description: Taller step ladder. More difficult overhead reach.

H4_SCAFFOLD.description: Full scaffold or lift. Significant access setup.

height_modifiers.application_rule: Engine applies height modifier per room via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND. NOT embedded in base rates. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ height_modifier. Height modifier applies ON TOP of the overhead penalty already baked into base rates. Combined effect at H3 with coffered: base_rate ÷ 1.5 (height) ÷ 1.35 (coffered) = very slow production.
height_modifiers.notes: ALL ceiling work starts overhead (even H1 requires step ladder). Height modifiers from Modifier_Registry v1.2. Key distinction from wood wall: wall work at H1 is standing floor work (no overhead), but ceiling work at H1 is already overhead.

quality_tier_modifiers.does_not_apply_to: application tasks and binary tasks — application quality is NOT tiered
quality_tier_modifiers.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ modifier. QT modifiers apply ONLY to qt_scaled tasks.

ceiling_style_modifier.application_rule: Modifiers increase TIME. effective_rate = base_rate ÷ modifier. Apply to ALL qt_scaled tasks and to application tasks (spray_finish, brush_finish, prime_faces, caulk_joints, seal_mdf_edges, sand_prep, sand_primer). Does NOT apply to protection, cleanup, or FIXED tasks.
ceiling_style_modifier.notes: flat_plank=baseline (simple boards). beadboard=narrow boards with bead groove detail (1.15x). tongue_and_groove=interlocking boards with tight joints (1.10x). coffered=beam+panel system with inside corners and multiple orientation changes (1.35x).

estimation_notes.overhead_penalty: ALL tasks in this spec are performed overhead. Base rates are ~0.70-0.80x of equivalent SF_WOOD_WALL_NC rates. The overhead penalty is BAKED INTO base rates — it is NOT a separate modifier. Spray tasks use ~0.75-0.78x (spray ergonomics are slightly better overhead). Brush tasks use ~0.70x (brush overhead is more fatiguing). Fixed-time tasks are ~1.25-1.33x longer (inverse of 0.75-0.80). Floor-level tasks (protection, cleanup, vacuum) use same rates as wood wall.
estimation_notes.sf_based: All wood ceiling tasks use SF as primary UOM. SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_CEILING. EA for fixture masking. FIXED for per-room/per-cycle overhead tasks.
estimation_notes.ceiling_style_impact: Coffered adds ~35% time due to beam faces, inside corners, and multiple orientation changes. Beadboard adds ~15% due to narrow board bead groove detail. T&G adds ~10% due to tight joint detail. Flat_plank is baseline.
estimation_notes.height_impact: Height modifier applies ON TOP of overhead base rates. H1 (8-9 ft) is already overhead work (step ladder needed). Combined example: 14 ft coffered ceiling QT4 inspection = 150 ÷ 1.5 (H3) ÷ 1.35 (coffered) ÷ 1.3 (QT4) = ~57 SF/hr.
estimation_notes.spray_vs_brush: Spray ~2.6x faster than brush at flat_plank (130 vs 50 SF/hr). The spray advantage is even more pronounced overhead than on walls because spray ergonomics are better overhead (arm extension vs brush overhead). Brush overhead is the most fatiguing application method.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. Refer to manufacturer PDS. Note: warm air at ceiling level may reduce dry times for ceiling surfaces.
estimation_notes.caulk_rate_basis: Internal caulk rate ~0.70x of wood wall due to overhead caulking difficulty. Beadboard ~30 SF/hr, T&G ~32 SF/hr, flat_plank ~35 SF/hr, coffered ~30 SF/hr. Perimeter caulk 90 SF/hr (0.75x of wall 120 SF/hr).

assumptions.value: 130 SF/hr for flat_plank wood ceiling spray finish
assumptions.source: Wood wall spray rate (175 SF/hr) × 0.75 overhead penalty
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wood-ceiling-specific SF spray rates. Derived from SF_WOOD_WALL_NC with overhead penalty.

assumptions.value: 50 SF/hr for flat_plank wood ceiling brush finish
assumptions.source: Wood wall brush rate (70 SF/hr) × 0.70 overhead penalty (more severe for brush)
assumptions.note: Brush overhead is more fatiguing than spray overhead — used 0.70x instead of 0.75x.

assumptions.source: Brief Section 13, adapted from Millwork Doctrine §7.2
assumptions.note: Coffered (1.35x) is higher than library_panel wall (1.25x) because coffered adds beam faces and inside corners with multiple orientation changes.

assumptions.value: 0.70-0.80x of equivalent wood wall rates, varies by task type
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides explicit overhead penalty. Spray uses 0.75-0.78x, brush uses 0.70x, sanding uses 0.75x. Field validation recommended.
Standard height modifiers. Key: H1 for ceiling is already overhead (step ladder needed), unlike H1 for walls (standing floor work).

assumptions.source: Research RF-015 — overhead caulking is significantly harder
assumptions.note: Overhead caulking has more severe penalty than other overhead tasks due to gravity pulling caulk from joints.
